title: fix(pm): derive the mandatory model tier from the card's file surface
body:
Fixes #8640

`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` derived the gate families a card's file surface moves, and said nothing about the model tier that same surface **mandates**. So the tier stayed the one recalled value in the claim comment — and a card whose surface included `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md` was claimed as "not under the fable-mandatory roots" and dispatched at opus. One sentence flowed unchecked from claim to dispatch to model choice, caught only at PR time by a downstream seat.

This makes the tier derived, in the same file, from the same argv.

## What landed

**1. `MANDATORY_TIER_GLOBS` — the policy's path half, as data.** One entry today: `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` (references included) ⇒ `claude-fable-5`, carrying the tier it mandates and the reason. The script header stays the authority on what the tool promises; the maintainer ruling quoted in the PM dispatch skill stays the authority on the policy, and the table says so — when they disagree, the skill wins and the table is the thing to fix.

**2. `deriveTier()` / `tierLines()`, matched with `hintCovers`.** One path-comparison rule in this file rather than two, so a glob gets segment-boundary semantics for free. The matcher's asymmetry (an input that is an **ancestor** of the glob counts as a hit) is the *correct* direction here, and the header argues why the two halves of this file legitimately want opposite error directions: an over-matched gate pastes a wrong command into a prompt; an under-mandated tier crosses a maintainer guardrail and is only visible afterwards.

**3. The verdict prints on EVERY run, hit or not** — plus a `--tier` flag that answers the claim-time question alone (it reads no workflow and no check script, so it still answers on a tree where the gate derivation cannot run). Printing only on a hit would make the line's absence mean two things at once: "no mandate" and "this build has no tier derivation".

```
$ node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md
Model tier — MANDATORY: claude-fable-5 (derived from the file surface, not recalled).
  - .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/review-checklist.md ⇢ '.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**' — clause ① …
  The only exit is the measured quota exemption (fable unavailable ⇒ opus, never lower), recorded with its
  reason in the claim comment's `Container & model` line.
  Clause ② is NOT reachable from paths: … This line is a FLOOR, never a clearance.
```

**4. Two refusals, in the shape of the residue partition guard.** A verdict whose parts contradict each other (a hit with no mandate, a mandate with no hit) is never rendered — that is the card's invariant made mechanical. Two globs mandating **different** tiers for one surface are refused rather than guessed between: this file orders no tiers.

**5. Live guards on the table.** Every declared glob must name a path this tree really has — a renamed skill root would otherwise leave dead data that mandates nothing while reading as protection, which is the incident class itself. Same census-guard shape `CHANGE_KIND_GATES` already carries.

## What this deliberately does NOT do

Clause ② of the mandatory-tier policy (a card that changes contract accept/reject behaviour or widens the public surface is fable-mandatory too) is **judged from card content, not paths**, and an ordinary-looking surface is the normal shape of such a card. Encoding a path heuristic for it would produce this file's own failure mode one level up: a "no mandate" line read as a clearance. So the no-mandate output names the clause it checked *and* the clause it cannot reach, on every run, and both renderings call the answer a FLOOR.

Shape 2 of the card (a report-only checker for a claim comment whose recorded tier contradicts the surface) is not here: it needs the comment text, which is not an input this tool has, so it was not the cheap in-file extension the grading allowed for.

## Measured side effect, recorded rather than left to be discovered

Comment masking cannot reach a module-body string, so the glob is now a watch hint of this file's own source: `extractWatchHints` yields 5 hints here against 4 on the base. Inert today — no check family resolves to this file; `check:pm-dispatch-gates` resolves to `check-dispatch-gates.mjs` and matches this file through that file's one constant. The note is in the table's docblock so the cost reads as known, not unnoticed.

## Verification — all at `82bbc6217`, the final commit

```
node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test    159 cases pass  (136 on origin/main, +23)
pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates                      exit 0   (the derived gate for this file surface)
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs --self-test      75 assertions pass
node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs                  OK, 5938 text files, no control bytes
npx eslint scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs          exit 0
pnpm check:pm-half-states                         exit 0
pnpm check:pm-skill-id-lint                       exit 0
pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet                       exit 0
pnpm check:ratchet-remedy-authority               exit 0
pnpm check:partof-closing-keyword                 exit 0
```

Gate union re-derived from the actual changed path with the post-change script: `check:pm-dispatch-gates` is the only path-matched family, and no convention kind hits (the changed file is not a test file; the type-check ratchets cannot reach a `.mjs` file, as the sibling PR measured). `skip-changeset`: scripts-only, releases nothing — same treatment as the sibling PR on this file, whose Check Changeset passed under that label.

Reverse verification, each direction predicted before running, restored byte-identically after (checking the file back out of the committed branch — never `git stash` — and verified with `diff -q`):

| ablation | predicted | observed |
|:--|:--|:--|
| the mandatory table emptied | 10 red — every mandate case and the non-vacuity guard; the ambiguity refusal (injected globs) and the clause-② line stay green | 10 red, exactly those. The ablated tool answers the incident surface with "no path-derived mandate" — the incident's own sentence, reproduced mechanically |
| `hintCovers` replaced by a raw prefix over the glob **as written** | 2 red | **1 red** — the prediction was wrong: the glob's own trailing `/**` already carries the boundary, so only the ancestor direction moved |
| raw prefix over the **collapsed** glob (the real sibling-prefix shape) | 2 red — the sibling directory and the ancestor surface | 2 red, exactly those |

The second row is reported as observed rather than as predicted: the segment matcher is load-bearing for the ancestor direction on its own, and for the sibling direction only once the glob is collapsed — which is precisely the comparison `hintCovers` performs internally.
